nodes.label: Booking & Appointment Management System (MVP)
nodes.author: AmmarDw
nodes.rationale: Chosen from model #1 of the AI MVP Bootcamp brochure; scope = user registration, service/appointment display, booking management from a dashboard, and confirmation notification.

nodes.label: conversation_history.md Document Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth surviving context-window limits, session resets and model switches; chat stays a minimal pointer, all prompts/responses live in the file.

nodes.label: PROJECT_REPORT.md (single graded deliverable)
nodes.rationale: One report with TOC: instructions -> template -> generic example -> actual booking-system data, so trainees see both the pattern and a filled example.

nodes.label: research_plan.md (research spikes R1-R4)
nodes.rationale: Registered spikes: R1 Google Meet feasibility, R2 admin dashboard patterns, R3 landing-page sections, R4 calendar UX.

nodes.label: .claude/rules/bootcamp-mvp-process.md
nodes.rationale: Deliberately kept generic so any bootcamp trainee project can use it to guide Claude.

nodes.label: Global i18n + directionality rule
nodes.rationale: Improved, context7-verified rewrite of the legacy i18n_context_system.md blueprint, promoted to a global rule file.

nodes.label: AI_MVP_Bootcamp_6_Days_AR.pdf
nodes.rationale: 6 days / 36h, teams of 2-3, 3-5 core features, demo data only; evaluation weights drive what the docs emphasise.

nodes.label: Lightweight, audience-appropriate documentation stance
nodes.rationale: Target audience is entrepreneurs/students/beginner-intermediate devs, not experts; the capstone report is a style reference only, never a depth target.

nodes.label: User entity (single entity with role field)
nodes.rationale: A separate Provider entity was dropped: one User + a role field (CONSUMER/PROVIDER/ADMIN) covers every case without duplicating identity.

nodes.label: UserService N:M (which services a provider offers)
nodes.rationale: Implemented as a plain @ManyToMany rather than a junction entity, since the join table carries no extra columns.

nodes.label: Service entity
nodes.rationale: Class name intentionally matches the domain/ERD term even though it collides with Spring's @Service annotation; the project sidesteps this by using @Component for business beans.

nodes.label: GoogleAccountConnection entity
nodes.rationale: Holds userId, googleEmail, encrypted refresh token, scope, connectedAt and a nullable fallbackMeetUrl so a provider is bookable either via OAuth or a pasted persistent link.

nodes.label: AppSettings (single-row typed settings table)
nodes.rationale: application.yaml is read once at startup, packaged in the JAR and often on a read-only filesystem, so it cannot hold a live admin-editable value; a single-row typed table seeded from the yaml default and cached in memory gives one row, one cached read, restart-survival and immediate effect. Live value is cached in memory and refreshed on admin update (AppSettingsCache), so the hot path is one cached read.

nodes.label: Rejected: generic SystemSetting key/value table
nodes.rationale: Over-engineered for a single value; replaced by the typed single-row AppSettings after the user pushed back on adding a whole key/value table for one setting.

nodes.label: Core rule: availability binds to the provider, not the service
nodes.rationale: A provider with 5 daily slots offering 5 services must not appear to have 25 appointments; booking one slot under any service marks it reserved across all that provider's services.

nodes.label: uq_provider_slot uniqueness constraint
nodes.rationale: DB-level enforcement of the one-slot-per-provider-per-time rule (FR-4) so overlapping duplicates cannot be created by any code path.

nodes.label: BookingStatus lifecycle (CONFIRMED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED/NO_SHOW/VACANT)
nodes.rationale: Cancel frees the slot back to AVAILABLE, no-show does not (moot anyway, since no-show only applies to past slots that cannot be rebooked); complete/no-show gate on the slot's END time, not its start.

nodes.label: VACANT as a synthesized, never-persisted status
nodes.rationale: A dashboard-only label for open AVAILABLE slots; the V7 CHECK constraint deliberately excludes it so it can never be written even though it is a Java enum value. Added by the V7 migration, whose CHECK constraint deliberately omits VACANT.

nodes.label: PATCH /api/bookings/{id}/status role + time gates
nodes.rationale: Enforces role (consumer cancels own >24h out; provider/admin completes after end), time gates, and only-from-CONFIRMED so terminal states are final (409). The UI shadows disallowed buttons but the server is the real gate.

nodes.label: Public landing page
nodes.rationale: Hero -> How-it-works/journey -> Services preview -> FAQ -> Footer; no social-proof section because an MVP has no proof to show.

nodes.label: /book service browsing page (public)
nodes.rationale: Browsing is open; clicking Book when logged out redirects to /sign-in?redirect=/book/{id} so the user returns to exactly where they were. Filtering is a single client-side service-name search box above the grid; no backend query is needed at this scale.

nodes.label: Decision: dedicated booking page, not a modal (R4)
nodes.rationale: The flow is multi-step, the URL should be shareable, and a real route makes the sign-in redirect-back clean.

nodes.label: /dashboard shared provider + admin dashboard
nodes.rationale: Same UI for both roles; admin gets extra provider filter/selector. Providers see only their own data, admins see everything. Includes a bookings-over-time chart and a 42-cell (6x7) calendar-aligned month grid sharing one Month/Week/Day granularity toggle, plus role-aware nav.

nodes.label: /appointments 'My Appointments' (consumer-only)
nodes.rationale: Briefly opened to all roles, then reverted to consumer-only: providers/admins already see their own consumer-side bookings merged into /dashboard, so a second page would duplicate data. Direct navigation by a provider/admin redirects to /dashboard.

nodes.label: /dashboard/connect-google provider onboarding screen
nodes.rationale: Three states: not-connected (Connect button + fallback-link paste + not-bookable warning), connected (account email/badge/Disconnect), and a compact dashboard warning banner variant.

nodes.label: Rule: one Claude Design prompt = one screen
nodes.rationale: The combined 'Connect Google + Services mgmt' prompt confused Claude Design about whether to produce one or two artefacts; splitting into single-screen prompts fixed it.

nodes.label: Stacked provider dropdowns for slot selection
nodes.rationale: Chosen over unified admin-defined slots and over a flat time-ordered stack: each provider is a dropdown, several can be open at once to compare, and the list scrolls gracefully as providers grow.

nodes.label: Calendar pressure colouring (high/medium/low/none)
nodes.rationale: Thresholds: >=4 available = low pressure (green), 3 = medium (amber), 1-2 = about to run out; colours derive from the site palette so they do not disrupt it, reinforced by the number badge and opacity for colourblind safety.

nodes.label: CalendarDayCell design-system component
nodes.rationale: Extended with an optional backward-compatible `total` prop, and later a `full` state so fully-booked days keep their 0/N badge and stay clickable instead of looking empty. Renders the available/total count badge (e.g. 3/8) that FR-9 requires.

nodes.label: Booking success toast (exact text pattern)
nodes.rationale: Auto-dismisses after ~30s with an x to close early. After the redirect change it is carried across via query params which are cleared immediately (router.replace) so a refresh does not re-show it.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay (blurred full-page wait)
nodes.rationale: The Book button triggers a synchronous Google Calendar + email round-trip that is slow enough to feel broken; the page blurs but never disappears so the user keeps context.

nodes.label: '(You)' marker on merged consumer-side rows
nodes.rationale: Only meaningful where the consumer field varies row-to-row, which /appointments can never be; so provider/admin self-bookings merge into /dashboard and render bold + primary-teal with a trailing (You) so they do not read as a real patient.

nodes.label: Provider cannot book their own availability
nodes.rationale: Enforced twice: the signed-in provider's own entry is filtered out of the day-view list client-side, and BookingService rejects it with 400 before any DB write because the client-side filter is not trusted.

nodes.label: Shared AppointmentDetailsModal
nodes.rationale: One details view wired into both the consumer /appointments table and the provider/admin dashboard table, rather than two near-duplicate modals; it is the only place the meeting link is surfaced.

nodes.label: Admin-configurable max booking horizon (default 6 months)
nodes.rationale: Bounds how far ahead consumers can book and keeps the year picker down to 1-2 years and the month grid meaningfully shadowed; enforced in both the calendar UI and server-side booking validation.

nodes.label: Provider advance limit = ceil(horizon x 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over doubling: +50% (6 -> 9 months) lets providers pre-load availability ahead of the consumer window without a second admin-facing setting; yaml-only multiplier derived from the admin horizon, and the rolling window makes pre-loaded slots bookable as time advances.

nodes.label: Decision: weekends are not special
nodes.rationale: Hard Fri/Sat skipping was removed because providers already pick weekdays explicitly and some may deliberately work weekends as a part-time job; calendar shadowing is now driven purely by having 0 available slots.

nodes.label: Bulk availability generator (weekdays x date range x time ranges)
nodes.rationale: Available to providers (own slots) and admins (any provider); idempotent re-runs skip existing slots and are bounded by the advance limit.

nodes.label: Decision: bulk generation is non-destructive
nodes.rationale: A deliberate deviation from the Claude Design copy that said 'conflicts will be replaced' — overwriting would risk deleting already-booked slots.

nodes.label: Decision: provider onboarding is admin-managed (FR-16)
nodes.rationale: Public sign-up always yields CONSUMER; only an admin creates providers or promotes a consumer. Consistent with the admin-controlled services model and gives better vetting; a crafted sign-up requesting PROVIDER is a privilege-escalation attempt and still yields CONSUMER.

nodes.label: Decision: no provider filter on the services grid
nodes.rationale: The journey is service-first: providers only become a filtering concept after a service and date are chosen, and provider-first browsing is unscoped new work, not in FR-1.

nodes.label: Monorepo layout (app/backend + app/frontend)
nodes.rationale: One Git repository holding both halves rather than two repos; the nested .git created by create-next-app was removed to keep it single-repo.

nodes.label: GitHub repo AmmarDw/booking-system
nodes.author: AmmarDw
nodes.rationale: Created private, with no README/.gitignore/license init so it would not conflict with the Spring-Initializr-generated files already present locally.

nodes.label: R1 — Google Meet link generation feasibility
nodes.rationale: Feasible on a free Gmail via Google Calendar API + OAuth2 (conferenceData.createRequest, hangoutsMeet); the 'Workspace only' claim applies to the Admin-SDK path, not user OAuth. Custom UI is preserved because the link comes back as a plain string.

nodes.label: R4 — Calendar UX (popup vs dedicated page)
Decision: per-provider Google connection from the start
nodes.rationale: Google marks anyone on the event guest list as Trusted so a single host account would not strictly force manual admits — but that model puts every meeting on an absent operator's calendar and any edge case (different email, waiting room on) could only be cleared by them. Per-provider gives correct ownership and better UX. The userinfo.email scope was added beyond the original spec so the connect screen can show which Google account is connected.

nodes.label: Fallback: provider pastes a persistent personal Meet link
nodes.rationale: A provider is not bookable until they either connect Google or set a fallback link; the fallback keeps the booking flow usable without OAuth.

nodes.label: Spring Boot 4.1.0 backend
nodes.rationale: Docs originally said 'Spring Boot 3'; the Initializr default turned out to be 4.1.0 with 4.x starter names, and the docs were reconciled to reality rather than the plan.

nodes.label: Stateless JWT Bearer authentication
nodes.rationale: Chosen with the user over session auth; security/ package holds JwtService, JwtAuthenticationFilter, AppUserDetailsService, UserPrincipal and CurrentUser. Sits on a stateless Spring Security chain with BCrypt and method security enabled.

nodes.label: SecurityConfig filter chain
nodes.rationale: Needs explicit .exceptionHandling(...) entry points — without them an unauthenticated request has no AuthenticationEntryPoint and surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of 401/403.

nodes.label: Bug: /api/auth/** permitAll leaked /me
nodes.rationale: The wildcard matcher also permitted /api/auth/me, so an anonymous request reached the controller and threw IllegalStateException from CurrentUser.get() instead of a clean 401. Fixed by naming /register and /login explicitly.

nodes.label: GlobalExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice)
nodes.rationale: A bare @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) with no logging silently converted real bugs into opaque 500s; logging was added so that class of bug cannot hide again.

nodes.label: Gotcha: @PreAuthorize denials need their own handler
nodes.rationale: Method-security throws AccessDeniedException inside the MVC handler invocation, so it never reaches SecurityConfig's filter-level accessDeniedHandler; without a dedicated @ExceptionHandler it falls into the catch-all as a 500 instead of 403.

nodes.label: Gotcha: void @DeleteMapping returns 200 + empty body
nodes.rationale: The frontend api() helper only special-cased 204 before calling res.json(), so a successful delete surfaced as a UI error. Fixed on both ends: deletes return ResponseEntity.noContent(), and api() checks response text before parsing regardless of status.

nodes.label: Gotcha: stale inverse-side @ManyToMany in the first-level cache
nodes.rationale: After updating the owning side (User.services) and re-fetching Service in the same persistence context, Hibernate returned the already-loaded instance with a stale providers collection. Fixed by building the response from the known-new set instead of re-querying.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Jackson 3 relocation (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper compiles but throws NoClassDefFoundError at runtime on this stack. Framework-managed JSON is unaffected; fixed by hand-writing the small fixed-shape JSON in the security layer rather than depending on Jackson there at all.

nodes.label: Convention: @Component, never @Service
nodes.rationale: Any class importing the Service entity cannot also import org.springframework.stereotype.Service under its simple name; using @Component everywhere sidesteps the clash uniformly instead of fully-qualifying case by case.

nodes.label: Flyway schema migrations
nodes.rationale: Flyway owns the schema; ddl-auto switched from update to validate so Hibernate only checks that entities match the migrated schema.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Spring Boot 4 moved FlywayAutoConfiguration into its own module
nodes.rationale: A bare flyway-core + flyway-database-postgresql never triggers autoconfiguration — it fails silently, so Flyway had never actually run and the earlier 'migrations applied' claim was unverifiable (no entities existed yet, so validate had nothing to check). Fixed with spring-boot-starter-flyway, keeping flyway-database-postgresql explicit since it is optional inside the starter.

nodes.label: Demo seed migrations (V2-V6)
nodes.rationale: Demo data only per the bootcamp rule. Bcrypt hashes were extracted from real registrations through the app's own /api/auth/register so they are guaranteed encoder-compatible, rather than hand-computed; a demo admin was seeded as a bootstrapping requirement since only an admin can create users.

nodes.label: Native Windows PostgreSQL 16 service (dev)
nodes.rationale: Docker was planned, but port 5432 was already occupied by an existing native service, so the native install was used instead. DB booking_system is owned by bookingadmin — ownership alone grants public-schema rights on PG15+, so no extra GRANTs are needed.

nodes.label: spring-dotenv (springboot4-dotenv) for local secrets
nodes.rationale: Auto-loads .env as a Spring property source in dev while real environment variables still take precedence, so it stays safe in production and needs no manual shell exports locally.

nodes.label: Rule: real values in .env, placeholders only in .env.example
nodes.rationale: The real DB password had been put in .env.example, which is committed by design; only .env is git-ignored. Caught before the project was even a git repo, so no history needed scrubbing.

nodes.label: Gotcha: spring-dotenv loads .env from the process working directory
nodes.rationale: ./mvnw runs from app/backend so it worked, but IntelliJ ran from a different directory, leaving DB_PASSWORD empty -> SCRAM auth failure -> 'Unable to determine Dialect' as a downstream symptom. Fix: set the run config working directory to app/backend.

nodes.label: BookingService (createBooking)
nodes.rationale: @Transactional; validates slot AVAILABLE, within the booking window, that the provider actually offers the requested service, and that the provider is not booking themselves — then flips the slot to BOOKED. Meeting-link and email failures can never fail the booking itself (NFR-4).

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE slot row lock
nodes.rationale: findByIdForUpdate row-locks the slot so two concurrent bookings cannot both see it as AVAILABLE.

nodes.label: Availability month/day endpoints
nodes.rationale: month returns per-day available/total counts; day returns providers grouped with their slots, including only providers with at least one slot that day.

nodes.label: GET /api/settings/booking-window (public)
nodes.rationale: Exposes maxHorizonMonths/today/maxBookableDate (later advanceLimitMonths/maxAdvanceDate) so the frontend can bound calendar navigation without trusting the client clock.

nodes.label: AppointmentQueryService (role-scoped listing)
nodes.rationale: Consumers are hard-scoped server-side to their own consumerUserId so filter params like providerId cannot be used to escape the scope; providers see their provider-scoped rows unioned with bookings they made as a consumer elsewhere. Exposed to the frontend as GET /api/bookings?mine=true, which always returns just the caller's own consumer-side bookings regardless of role.

nodes.label: GET /api/bookings/{feed,stats,chart}
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated multi-value serviceIds/statuses/providerIds plus from/to date range; feed adds synthesized VACANT entries with a negative id and null consumer.

nodes.label: Four date-range-driven stat cards
nodes.rationale: The date range fully replaces the fixed today/this-week/30d windows and the labels adapt. Cards are narrowed by service+provider but deliberately not by the status filter, since each card has an intrinsic status meaning (a no-show rate needs completed+no_show regardless).

nodes.label: Shared dashboard filter system
nodes.rationale: Service / Status / Provider (admin-only) multi-selects plus a date range, applied uniformly to every section so no view can silently show a different slice.

nodes.label: EmailService (Gmail SMTP confirmations)
nodes.rationale: Never throws, per NFR-4. Sends two mails per booking: the consumer confirmation (naming provider name+email) and a separate provider notification (naming consumer name+email) so the provider knows without checking the dashboard. Gmail SMTP on port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS, and the nested spring.mail properties must be written as bracket-quoted YAML keys.

nodes.label: GoogleCalendarService#createMeetingEvent
nodes.rationale: events.insert with conferenceDataVersion=1, hangoutsMeet createRequest, attendees=[consumer, provider] and sendUpdates=all, on the provider's own calendar so they are the organiser who actually attends. Returns null on any failure rather than throwing.

nodes.label: GoogleOAuthService / GoogleOAuthController
nodes.rationale: authorize builds the consent URL with prompt=consent so a refresh token is issued even on reconnect; the callback is public because Google redirects the browser there with no Authorization header.

nodes.label: OAuth state as a short-lived signed JWT
nodes.rationale: Google's callback is a plain browser redirect with no Authorization header, so the JWT filter cannot tell which provider initiated it; a 10-minute purpose-tagged token carrying the provider's user id, signed with the existing key, is the only way to identify them.

nodes.label: Gotcha: OAuth callback params must be optional
nodes.rationale: A provider clicking Cancel on the consent screen redirects back with error=access_denied and no code param at all; required @RequestParams turned the single most common non-happy path into a raw 500. Caught by deliberately curling that exact shape, not by review.

nodes.label: TokenCipher (AES-256-GCM refresh-token encryption)
nodes.rationale: Key derived via SHA-256 of TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY so any non-empty configured string yields a valid 256-bit key.

nodes.label: Google Cloud project + OAuth client setup (U4)
nodes.rationale: The console is console.cloud.google.com — guessed Google subdomains are a phishing pattern. The 'External' tab no longer exists in the new Google Auth Platform UI (it is the Audience setting from the Get Started wizard), and the redirect URI is a text value pasted into Google's form, not a page to visit.

nodes.label: Next.js 16 App Router frontend
nodes.rationale: create-next-app default installed 16 / React 19 / Tailwind v4, reconciling the docs that had said 14 — the same reality-over-plan correction made for Spring Boot. AGENTS.md warns it differs from training data; check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing page code.

nodes.label: BookIt design system (src/components/ds)
nodes.rationale: Tokens (availability-pressure colours, teal, light/dark, Arabic RTL typography swap) plus 11 ES-module components with a barrel export; the 4 Claude Design screens are kept as visual reference only because they rely on sandbox globals rather than ES imports. Primary token is teal #0D9488, with availability greens/ambers tuned distinct and reinforced by the number badge and opacity for colourblind safety.

nodes.label: Claude Design (design generation tool)
nodes.rationale: Design-System-first, then a separate generation per screen selecting that system — never in the system's own chat and never reusing one screen's chat, so iteration history from one screen cannot bleed into another.

nodes.label: DesignSync (Claude Design -> repo bridge)
nodes.rationale: The /design-sync skill is user-triggered only and cannot be model-invoked, so components were pulled via the DesignSync tool's get_file plus local writes.

nodes.label: Gotcha: DS component hooks without "use client"
nodes.rationale: Accordion.jsx calls React.useState internally but shipped without the directive, so rendering it from the Server Component landing page threw 'useState is not a function' at build time. Fixed at the component, not worked around at the page.

nodes.label: Gotcha: public DB-backed pages need force-dynamic
nodes.rationale: The landing page built as a static route, baking in whatever the backend returned at build time; export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' makes the services preview live.

nodes.label: Gotcha: toLocaleDateString(undefined) uses the OS locale
nodes.rationale: Rendered Arabic month names on a machine with an Arabic OS locale even though no i18n was wired up; always pass an explicit 'en-US' until real i18n exists.

nodes.label: Gotcha: avoid native number/date/time inputs
nodes.rationale: Chromium renders them with the OS locale, producing Arabic-Indic digits and Arabic day/month labels; replaced with type=text plus format placeholders and regex validation. Kept deliberately even where the Claude Design source used native pickers.

nodes.label: src/lib/api.ts fetch wrapper
nodes.rationale: Injects the Bearer token and checks response text before JSON.parse regardless of status, so a 200-with-empty-body cannot throw.

nodes.label: src/lib/auth.tsx (AuthProvider / useAuth)
nodes.rationale: Token store with localStorage persistence; later threaded the user's id through so the UI can answer 'is this row's consumer me' and 'is this provider me'.

nodes.label: Redirect-back after sign-in (?redirect=)
nodes.rationale: FR-2: an unauthenticated user who tries to book is sent to sign-in and returned to exactly the booking flow they were on.

nodes.label: M6.1 — Provider email, My Appointments, details modal
M6.2 — Redirect, richer emails, overlay, self-booking guard
M6.3 — Claude Design fidelity pass (6 phases)
nodes.rationale: Grounded in the actual Claude Design source fetched via DesignSync for all five linked pages rather than guessed, with four clarifying questions answered before any code.

nodes.label: context7 MCP (up-to-date library docs)
nodes.rationale: Standing rule to verify library APIs rather than rely on training data; still not infallible — its own indexed jjwt snippet was stale for the installed version.

nodes.label: chrome-devtools MCP (live browser testing)
nodes.rationale: Every milestone is browser-verified, not just claimed; screenshots and network inspection caught bugs the a11y tree and code review both missed.

nodes.label: Practice: verify against running systems, never just claim
nodes.rationale: Repeatedly decisive: the silent Flyway failure, the stale-cache empty response, the 200-vs-204 delete and a false-positive auth gate (a leftover JWT in localStorage) were all only findable by exercising the real system.

nodes.label: drawio skill unreachable from Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Claude Code uses a separate skill registry (~/.claude/skills/ + plugins) from the Desktop app's uploaded-skills store; .drawio is plain XML so the diagrams were authored directly instead.

nodes.label: diagrams/consumer_booking_activity.drawio
nodes.rationale: Two swimlanes (Consumer blue, System green as a stakeholder) with orange decision nodes — the user's 'timeline per stakeholder' idea kept deliberately simple.

nodes.label: diagrams/erd.drawio (8 entities)
nodes.rationale: Laid out from the actual live Flyway V1 schema rather than re-derived from the report's prose, so the diagram matches what is really running.

nodes.label: RBAC enforcement + security review practice
nodes.rationale: Verified by deliberately attempting unauthorized access: cross-provider ownership guards, admin-only endpoints returning 403, consumer scope that cannot be escaped via filter params, and the FR-16 privilege-escalation attempt.

hyperedges.label: End-to-end booking transaction: slot lock -> validation -> Meet link -> dual email -> redirect + toast
hyperedges.rationale: One synchronous server-side flow whose latency is the reason the blurred overlay exists; integration failures (Meet, email) are contained so they can never fail the booking itself.

hyperedges.label: Two-window booking horizon: yaml default -> AppSettings row -> cache -> consumer horizon vs provider advance limit
hyperedges.rationale: A single admin-set duration fans out into two distinct rolling windows enforced in four places: calendar navigation, booking validation, bulk-generation bounds, and the public settings endpoint.

hyperedges.label: Per-provider Google onboarding: consent -> signed state -> encrypted refresh token -> Meet event, with fallback link gate
hyperedges.rationale: A public browser redirect carries no auth header, so identity travels in a signed state token; the provider becomes the event organiser who actually attends, and a provider with neither connection nor fallback is simply not bookable.
